extraction.name: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB)
extraction.description: A benchmark for text embeddings spanning 8 embedding tasks, 58 datasets, and 112 languages. It is designed to evaluate how embedding models perform across a wide variety of use cases and provides open-source software plus a public leaderboard.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.inLanguage: ara, cmn, deu, eng, fra, ita, pol, rus, spa, tur
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The Reddit clustering dataset was created for MTEB using available Reddit posts, clustering the concatenation of title and post by subreddit.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Available Reddit posts, specifically the concatenated title and post text labeled by subreddit.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential benchmark bias from overlap between some MTEB datasets and model training data (data contamination), which can inflate results for certain models on certain tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: No single embedding model works best across all tasks; benchmark results vary strongly by task and language. Controlling for training-data contamination is challenging and ignored in scores. Some multilingual models perform poorly on languages not seen in pre-training, and the default multilingual LASER2 model shows high variance across languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primarily benchmarking and evaluation of text embedding models across 8 tasks; evaluation is run mainly on test splits (except MSMARCO dev split). The benchmark is intended to help researchers and practitioners select embedding models for different downstream use cases such as clustering, search, retrieval, reranking, classification, STS, summarization, and bitext mining.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Open-source benchmark with public leaderboard, dataset/software versioning for reproducibility, published JSON result files, and ongoing community maintenance via pull requests and leaderboard submissions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data processing was run as part of the evaluations on the Jean Zay cluster of IDRIS.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: “On SciDocsRR (Cohan et al., 2020a) they perform far better than bigger models, which is likely due to parts of SciDocsRR being included in their training data. Our scale of experiments and that of model pre-training make controlling for data contamination challenging. Thus, we ignore overlap of MTEB datasets with model training datasets in MTEB scores.”

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: “We found model performance on different tasks to vary strongly with no model claiming state-of-the-art on all tasks.”
